How the agent behaves today, in plain language
What do you want to change? Tell the agent in plain words how it should behave differently
History of changes: who, when and a one-line summary, with undo on each change

ruleRefs.description: An agent's behavior is read, changed and undone only through the cm; this module never stores it.
Only the company admin may change or undo an agent's behavior.
Undoing a change from the behavior history brings back the behavior the agent had before that change, and the change is shown as undone.

organisms.text: The @name people use to call the agent in a chat, on or off, and the responsible person; you are told if another active agent already uses the name
The agent's limits as the cm lists them

ruleRefs.description: An agent's @name cannot be one already used by another active agent; the cm refuses it and the screen tells the admin the name is taken.

organisms.text: What the agent is, who it talks to, on whose behalf it acts and who is responsible for it
What it can: see which tools the agent can or cannot use and why, for yourself or, as admin, for a chosen person or role
What it understands: type a sentence and see whether it asks for an action, which part of the tree and which actions
Tools by module, subject and action with readable names and descriptions, when each was chosen and whether it was removed from the release; tick to turn an action on or off for this agent
Tools turned on automatically: suggested by a ready draft or chosen after a new release, never overriding your own choices

ruleRefs.description: Once the admin has turned a tool on or off for an agent, no automatic step changes that choice.
There is at most one on or off choice for each pair of agent and tool.
When the cm asks for an agent's tools, only the tools that are on for that agent are sent, each with its whole stored catalog item.
A tool choice that refers to a removed tool is shown as removed and never sent to the agent.
When the cm asks for an agent and a person, the tools that person may not use are left out of the tools returned.
A notice from the cm that has already been handled changes nothing when it arrives again.
The tools suggested in a ready draft are turned on for it as automatic choices, without changing any choice the admin already made.

New tools in the catalog are chosen automatically from each agent's description for every agent of the company, read from the cm, not only for agents that already have a tool choice; the admin may then adjust them.

When the cm asks this module to describe an agent for a person, the module only reads: it returns only the tools that are on for that agent, minus the tools that person may not use, each with its whole stored catalog item; it invents nothing and writes nothing.

When the admin marks an action the agent has no choice for yet, a new choice for that agent and that action is created as an admin choice; marking or unmarking an action that already has a choice only turns that choice on or off.
